response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, SUM(t.Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name) SELECT Name, rate, track_count, rate - (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM r) AS rate_above_average FROM r WHERE rate > (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM r)

assumptions.assumption: A media type's rate is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds across its tracks (ratio of sums), not an average of per-track ratios.
Track count includes every track of the media type, including any with NULL Bytes (those add nothing to the Bytes sum but their Milliseconds are still counted).
The inner join to MediaType leaves out media types with no tracks and tracks with no matching media type; the simple average is taken over the remaining media types, each counted once.

alternatives.interpretation: The rate is the mean of each track's own Bytes/Milliseconds ratio within the media type, rather than total Bytes over total Milliseconds.
